title: Smooth kernel-image decomposition for real elliptic operators
statement: All vector spaces below are over the real field $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth real manifold without boundary of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and its volume form. Let $E,F$ be smooth real vector bundles on $N$ of the same finite rank, each with a smooth positive definite fibre inner product. Write $\Gamma^\infty(E)$ and $\Gamma^\infty(F)$ for their real vector spaces of smooth sections, with $L^2$ inner products obtained by integrating the fibre inner products. Let $P:\Gamma^\infty(E)\to\Gamma^\infty(F)$ be a real-linear differential operator of order at most $k$, for some integer $k\geq1$, with smooth coefficients: in coordinates and bundle frames it has the form $\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}a_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$. Assume its degree-$k$ principal symbol (formed from the $|\alpha|=k$ coefficients) is invertible at every nonzero real cotangent vector. Let $P^*:\Gamma^\infty(F)\to\Gamma^\infty(E)$ be a differential operator with smooth coefficients satisfying $\langle Pu,v\rangle_{L^2}=\langle u,P^*v\rangle_{L^2}$ for all smooth sections. Then there is an orthogonal direct sum of real vector spaces $$\Gamma^\infty(E)=\ker P\ \mathbin{\oplus^{\perp}}\ P^*(\Gamma^\infty(F)).$$ In particular every smooth section $a$ can be written $a=h+P^*v$ with $h\in\Gamma^\infty(E)$, $Ph=0$, and $v\in\Gamma^\infty(F)$ smooth; the image in this statement is the actual image, with no closure.

source.place: WANTED locally: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025); read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf; §6.2 Theorem 6.5(4), printed p.23. Only its smooth orthogonal decomposition assertion is requested, in the real vector-bundle setting stated before the theorem.

proof.text: Put $Q=P^*$. In local smooth orthonormal frames, write $P=\sum a_\alpha\partial^\alpha$ and $dV=\rho\,dx$. Repeated integration by parts gives $Qv=\rho^{-1}\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}(-1)^{|\alpha|}\partial^\alpha(\rho a_\alpha^t v)$: the given adjoint equals this expression since their difference pairs to zero with every compactly supported smooth test section (test the difference against itself times a nonnegative cutoff). Consequently $Q$ has order at most $k$ and $\sigma_k(Q)=(-1)^k\sigma_k(P)^t$ is invertible. Symmetry of the real pairing also says that $P$ is the formal adjoint of $Q$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §1 (1.5)--(1.7), printed pp.288--289; local integration-by-parts calculation; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-elliptic-sobolev-closed-range] to $Q:F\to E$, which has the required ellipticity by step 1 and has the same compact base and metric equal-rank bundles. This gives a bounded extension $T_Q:H^k(F)\to L^2(E)$ with closed range $R$, and identifies its values with distributional $Q$. The cited completion statement also makes $L^2(E)$ a real Hilbert space and embeds $H^k(F)$ in $L^2(F)$ and distributions.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, first part of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: For a smooth $a$, apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-orthogonal-projection] in $L^2(E)$ to the closed linear subspace $R$. Obtain $a=r+h$ with $r\in R$ and $h\in R^\perp$, and choose $v\in H^k(F)$ with $T_Qv=r$. For any smooth $\phi\in\Gamma^\infty(F)$, the element $Q\phi=T_Q\phi$ belongs to $R$, hence $\langle h,Q\phi\rangle=0$. By the definition of distributional differentiation and the formal adjoint identity, $\langle Ph,\phi\rangle_{\mathcal D^{\prime},\mathcal D}=\langle h,Q\phi\rangle_{L^2}=0$; thus $Ph=0$ distributionally. Also $Qv=r=a-h$ distributionally.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, Corollary (2.4)(ii), equation (2.6), printed p.290; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-elliptic-adjoint-regularity] first to $P$ and the $L^2(E)$ section $h$: its right-hand side $0$ is smooth, so $h$ is smooth. Then $r=a-h$ is smooth. Apply the same node to $Q$ and $v\in H^k(F)\subseteq L^2(F)$, with smooth right-hand side $r$. Step 1 checked ellipticity of $Q$, so $v$ too is smooth. Distributional identities between smooth sections are the corresponding classical identities (their difference tested against itself has zero norm). We have obtained $a=h+P^*v$ with $Ph=0$ and both summands smooth.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2 (2.3), (2.1) and the end of Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed pp.289--290; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: For smooth $h\in\ker P$ and smooth $v$, $\langle h,P^*v\rangle=\langle Ph,v\rangle=0$. If a smooth $x$ lies in both summands, write $x=P^*v$ and use $Px=0$ to get $\|x\|_{L^2}^2=\langle Px,v\rangle=0$, hence $x=0$. Combined with spanning from step 4, this proves the asserted orthogonal direct sum with the actual smooth image. The summand $P^*v$ is unique; no uniqueness of its primitive $v$ is claimed.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, orthogonality in Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed p.290; elementary pairing argument; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof_origin.place: VI §§1--2, especially Corollary (2.4)(ii), printed pp.288--290; both local literature PDFs are WANTED. Applied to Q=P* to obtain Kong Theorem 6.5(4).
